rounds.text: Amit Securities Ltd is currently under-appreciated because its intrinsic value of Rs 41 per share sits above the market price of Rs 35.7, offering a margin of safety of 12.4% [E36, E37]. The business operates on a pristine balance sheet, maintaining a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and a highly comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 9.15x [E31, E32]. Operational momentum is turning a corner, evidenced by accelerating earnings growth, a 71% year-on-year surge in net profit, and a strong results score of 76 out of 100 that outpaces cautious market sentiment [E46, E48, E51]. Medium-term metrics also show resilience, with 5-year compounded sales growth at 19% and compounded profit growth at 26% [E15, E19]. Furthermore, today's price implies an earnings growth rate of only 16.5%, which is well within reach given the company's baseline trajectory [E38]. Conceded: the company carries a low return on equity of roughly 3.3% and generated negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.31 Cr in March 2026 [E13, E29, E44].

Amit Securities Ltd trades at an elevated valuation that is completely disconnected from its anemic operational returns, featuring a trailing price-to-earnings ratio of 36.2x to 42x against a sector benchmark of just 18.62x [E1, E6]. This premium multiple is severely undermined by a dismal profitability profile, demonstrated by a persistently low return on equity stuck at 3% to 3.3% across 1-year, 3-year, 5-year, and 10-year periods, lagging far behind the sector benchmark of 5.57% [E9, E13, E24, E25, E26, E27]. Furthermore, the business suffers from severe cash generation issues, delivering negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -0.31 Cr alongside a negative cash conversion ratio of -0.57x for Mar 2026 [E28, E29, E30]. Compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months has sharply contracted by -25%, while its 10-year compounded sales growth sits at -2%, highlighting long-term stagnation despite recent short-term bounce-backs [E14, E21]. Compounded share price growth over the past year reflects this underlying fundamental weakness with a steep decline of -39%, leaving the stock languishing at just 23% of its 52-week range [E5, E23]. Conceded: the company maintains a conservative balance sheet with zero debt, a strong current ratio of 9.15x, and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 26% [E19, E31, E32, E42].

Conceded: trailing valuation multiples stand above sector benchmarks [E1, E6, E7, E11] and return on equity sits at modest levels [E9, E13, E24, E25, E26, E27]. However, the valuation discount is bridged by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 41 per share against a market price of Rs 35.7, providing a margin of safety [E36, E37]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price implies only 16.5% earnings growth, which is lower than the base case assumption of 18.0% [E38]. Conceded: operating cash flow was negative for Mar 2026 [E28, E29, E30] and 10-year sales growth was negative [E14]. Yet, short-term momentum shows strong acceleration with a 5-year compounded sales growth of 19% [E15], a 5-year compounded profit growth of 26% [E19], and recent net profit surging by 71% YoY [E46]. Dismissing this turnaround on stale sentiment ignores that results are improving with a results score of 76/100, while the balance sheet remains exceptionally strong with zero debt and a comfortable current ratio of 9.15x [E31, E32, E42, E51].

Conceded: a discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 41 versus the market price of Rs 35.7 [E36], and a reverse DCF implies 16.5% earnings growth [E38]. However, that modest 12.4% margin of safety [E37] completely ignores catastrophic cash generation realities where operating cash flow and free cash flow both collapsed to negative Rs 0.31 Cr in March 2026, delivering a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -0.57x [E28, E29, E30]. The bull leans heavily on short-term sales and profit acceleration [E15, E19, E46], but glosses over a severe -25% collapse in trailing twelve-month compounded profit growth [E21] and a miserable 10-year compounded sales growth rate of -2% [E14]. Furthermore, defending the valuation via "zero debt" [E31, E42] is a hollow shield when the company delivers anemic, stagnant returns evidenced by a decade-long median return on equity stuck at a dismal 3% [E24, E25, E26, E27] and a trailing ROCE of just 0.9% [E12]. Finally, quoting a 76/100 results score to dismiss stale sentiment [E51] ignores the objective reality that the stock trades at an exorbitant EV/EBITDA of 189.01x against a sector benchmark of just 13.01x [E11], alongside a zero percent dividend yield [E4] that leaves minority shareholders empty-handed despite reported profits [E43].
